title: Egg omelet with cheese, meat, tomatoes, and dark‑green vegetables

content.title: About
content.content: A fluffy egg omelet enriched with cheese, tender meat, ripe tomatoes, and dark‑green vegetables such as spinach, broccoli, or kale. The dish is rich in high‑quality protein, B‑vitamins, vitamin K, and minerals like iron, calcium, and potassium. It works well as a hearty breakfast or a light dinner.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Eggs are one of the most affordable complete protein sources.
Cheese adds calcium and a creamy texture to the omelet.
Tomatoes provide the antioxidant lycopene, which supports heart health.
Dark‑green vegetables are packed with chlorophyll and vitamin K, important for blood clotting.
The protein‑fat combination makes the meal slowly digestible, keeping you full longer.

items.title: Muscle support
items.content: Protein from eggs and meat helps build and repair muscle tissue.

items.title: Bone health
items.content: Calcium from cheese and vitamin K from greens strengthen bone density.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Lycopene from tomatoes and chlorophyll from greens combat free radicals.

items.title: Immune boost
items.content: Vitamins A, C and the B‑complex enhance the body’s immune response.

items.title: Balanced energy
items.content: A mix of protein, fat, and complex carbs provides steady energy levels.

items.title: Egg or dairy allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to eggs, cheese, or milk may experience reactions.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Cheese and processed meat can be salty; people with hypertension should watch portions.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The dish is relatively calorie‑rich due to fats; portion control is advised for weight management.

items.title: Cholesterol levels
items.content: Eggs and meat contain cholesterol; those with elevated cholesterol should consume in moderation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the omelet hot, optionally garnished with fresh herbs, a drizzle of olive oil, or sliced avocado. It pairs well with whole‑grain toast, yogurt, or a light side salad.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Best enjoyed immediately. If needed, store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. Reheat in a skillet or microwave with a splash of oil to prevent drying out.
